facts.fact: The IGC policy brief states that in Zambia the prevailing use of manual systems and hard copy maps for administering property undermines councils' property tax revenue, and that most local councils still run on manual systems, with the few partly digitalised working in silos at department or section level; the date is the brief's own (May 2024).
facts.system: manual property rate administration (paper records, ledgers, receipt books)

facts.fact: The brief states that Lusaka City Council's property tax collection is based on manual systems, with no GIS tools in rates collection and hard copy maps used for bill distribution; the date is the brief's own (May 2024).
facts.system: Lusaka City Council manual rates collection

facts.fact: The brief names councils' weak capacity to administer property tax, partly from outdated cadastres and poor record keeping, with many tax maps covering only a fraction of rateable properties; date is the brief's own (May 2024).
facts.system: council property tax maps and valuation rolls

systems.owner: Ordnance Survey with IGC and Commonwealth Association of Architects
systems.tiers: Lusaka, 420 km2, 256,678 properties identified against about 82,000 on the 2019 valuation roll
Lusaka; not integrated into rates collection or the Valuation Department
